title: Wren and the Atlas
premise: In 1890s Ceylon, Lena Thackeray, indentured to the Meridian Trading Company since her pearl-diver father drowned, has survived by being unremarkable. When a gaunt stranger slips her a letter in her father's unmistakable hand—proof he lives and that the company's director murdered divers to seize their claims—she must carry it through three checkpoints to the colonial magistrate before the company's next shipment silences every witness. Betrayed at the second checkpoint by the friend she trusted most, Lena chooses truth over safety, exposing the director at the cost of her own anonymity and winning her father's freedom—and her own.
about_author: Cyrus Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trade ledgers from the Indian Ocean pearl fisheries. Their fiction draws on the forgotten voices found scrawled in the margins of those records.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. We meet her scrubbing ledgers in the Meridian counting house, invisible among clerks who never learn her name. A storm-battered stranger collapses at the dock gate and presses a salt-stained letter into her hands—her dead father's handwriting, naming Director Voss as a murderer. Emotional beat: fear cracking open into reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Three Gates
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She studies the letter by lamplight and maps her route: the harbor checkpoint, the customs house, the magistrate's court. Her closest friend, Devi, notices her distraction and swears loyalty. Voss announces an inspection that will move up the shipment—and the timeline. Emotional beat: quiet resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the harbor gate she talks her way past a suspicious sergeant, but at the customs house Devi betrays her for a promised release from indenture. Cornered in the warehouse district, Lena hides the letter inside a coil of diving rope from her father's old gear and flees through the night market. Emotional beat: heartbreak transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Atlas Opens
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, climaxing at the magistrate's court as Voss arrives to destroy the evidence. She produces the letter and names the drowned divers one by one; her father, alive and imprisoned on Voss's private island, is summoned as witness. Voss falls, the indentures are voided, and Lena signs her own name in the ledger for the first time. Emotional beat: grief, justice, and selfhood reclaimed.
